subject: maths
chapter_title: Predicting What Comes Next: Exploring Sequences and Progressions

concepts.title: Sequences and Their Rules
concepts.definition: A sequence is an ordered list of numbers following a rule; the explicit rule computes any term directly from its position n, while the recursive rule builds each term from the previous one - two ways of predicting what comes next.
concepts.key_idea: Position in, term out: an explicit rule jumps to any term without listing the rest.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh108.txt sections 8.1-8.3 (sequences, explicit and recursive rules)
question_patterns: write the next three terms of the given sequence
find the 10th term of the sequence with the given rule
write the explicit rule of the given sequence
write the recursive rule of the given sequence
which term of the sequence equals the given value
compare the explicit and recursive descriptions of a sequence

solution_steps.action: count the steps from the first term
solution_steps.explain: The nth term sits n minus 1 steps ahead.
Each step adds the common difference.

concepts.title: Arithmetic Progressions
concepts.definition: An arithmetic progression is a sequence whose consecutive terms differ by a fixed number d, the common difference; its nth term is a plus (n - 1)d, letting us jump to any term - like the 20th - without writing the nineteen before it.
concepts.key_idea: Constant difference d: the ladder of the progression, one d per step.
question_patterns: find the 15th term of the AP with first term 5 and common difference 3

write the nth term of the given arithmetic progression
find the first negative term of the given AP

solution_steps.explain: The nth term needs n minus 1 jumps of d.
Add steps times d to the first term.

concepts.title: Sum of the First n Natural Numbers
concepts.definition: Pairing terms from the two ends of 1 + 2 + ... + n shows each pair sums to n + 1, so the whole sum is n times (n + 1) over 2 - the classic triangular number formula that Gauss used as a schoolboy.
concepts.key_idea: Pair the ends: each pair adds n + 1, and there are n over 2 such pairs.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh108.txt section 8.5 (sum of the first n natural numbers)
question_patterns: find the sum of the first 20 natural numbers

solution_steps.explain: The product counts all paired contributions.
Each pair was counted twice, so divide by 2.

concepts.title: Geometric Progressions
concepts.definition: A geometric progression multiplies by a fixed ratio r at every step, so its nth term is the first term times r to the (n - 1); doubling sequences like 1, 2, 4, 8 are the classic case.
concepts.key_idea: Constant multiplier: r per step, applied n minus 1 times.
question_patterns: find the 6th term of the GP with first term 3 and ratio 2

solution_steps.explain: The nth term applies the ratio n minus 1 times.
Multiply the first term by r to the steps.
